html:
The Ciguayos were a people of the Samaná Peninsula and the north coast of Hispaniola, in today's Dominican Republic. They spoke their own language, different from that of the Taíno around them, and may have lived on the island before the Taíno farmers arrived. Almost nothing of their language survives.

In January 1493, at the end of his first voyage, Columbus anchored in the Bay of Samaná. His men clashed with Ciguayo archers, who wore their hair long and fought with bows, in the first armed fight of his voyages; he named the place the Gulf of Arrows. Within a few decades of the Spanish conquest of Hispaniola, war, forced labour and disease had wiped out the Ciguayos.
